summary.intent: Update Claude Code to the latest version using the recommended installation method, then run a full development retrospective to prune knowledge graph files, propagate metrics to core documentation, and persist learnings to SurrealDB and the Obsidian vault.
summary.outcome: Claude Code was migrated from npm/Linuxbrew (v2.1.105) to native installer (v2.1.112). The retrospective completed: KEY_LEARNINGS compressed 48% (382→197 lines), MISSION_JOURNAL updated with sessions 97-101, CLAUDE.md and CAPABILITY_MAP_REDUX.md refreshed with accurate metrics, SurrealDB crash loop fixed and learnings persisted, and 3 vault entries created.

repo: Skills have grown from 206 to 235 .md files (+14%) with 215 PRIME-format skills, but the skill_registry.json only has 133 entries — the registry is significantly stale and needs regeneration.
JEPA tests are 34 total (25 + 9), not 9 as CLAUDE.md claimed — a 3.7x undercount.
Genesis tests are 398 (physics + world_model + environments), not 348 as documented.
MCP tools are 87, not '41+' as documented — nearly double the claimed count.

SurrealDB has two separate graph systems: neurons/synapses (vault-keeper domain for Graph HIHO) and prompt_artifacts/universe_snapshots (genesis execution) — they are different namespaces and persist independently.
The journey_transitions and prompt_artifacts SurrealDB tables do not exist in the current DB namespace and may need schema migration.
Vault currently has 4 decisions, 3 patterns, and 0 experiments populated.
Ruff reports 4,307 pre-existing errors (2,368 auto-fixable) — no regressions introduced this session.
workflow: SurrealDB 3.0 requires --temporary-directory path to pre-exist; after /tmp cleanup or reboot the directory is gone, causing an exit-code-2 crash loop that triggers systemd rate limiting. Fix: mkdir -p /tmp/surrealdb + systemctl --user reset-failed surrealdb.service + start.
When systemd hits restart rate limits, systemctl start is blocked until reset-failed is called — standard restart alone is insufficient after a crash loop.
The ripgrep binary was bundled inside the npm Claude Code package; removing npm breaks the Grep tool for the current session. It self-heals after restarting with the native binary.
Claude Code native installer places the binary at ~/.local/bin/claude as a symlink to ~/.local/share/claude/versions/<version>, enabling zero-downtime auto-updates by re-pointing the symlink.
Two Claude Code installations can silently conflict — whichever appears first in $PATH wins, and switching shells or PATH ordering can silently drop back to an older version.
Metrics drift at roughly 2-4% per session without retrospective passes; compound engineering loop (retrospect → propagate → verify) is required to keep self-model accurate.

KEY_LEARNINGS compression strategy: merge verbose multi-paragraph entries for old sessions into single-line summaries while keeping recent sessions (85+) at full detail — temporal decay applied to documentation.
